item.title: Wakayama Food Guide: Mikan Oranges, Kishu Plums & Kuroshio Seafood
item.description: Wakayama Prefecture’s food identity is inseparable from its geography. The prefecture stretches from the mountains of Koyasan down through deep river valleys to a rugged Pacific coastline swept by the warm Kuroshio Current — one of the ocean’s great fish highways. The warm climate of the Kii Peninsula produces Japan’s finest citrus and most celebrated pickled plums, while the Kuroshio delivers bluefin tuna, spiny lobster, and skipjack caught by fishing fleets that have worked these waters for centuries.
